question: Why did the error rate go up on 07 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: Upstream search-cluster is returning HTTP 503 errors, causing service search error rate to spike.
why_chain: The upstream search-cluster is experiencing degraded performance, indicated by the HTTP 503 errors.
These errors are causing the service search to fail, resulting in an increase in error rate.
The error rate increase is observed in service search, with no change in request volume or latency.

contributing_factors.description: Service search has a high error rate increase, coinciding with upstream search-cluster issues.
why_chain: The error rate for service search has increased significantly, from 0.35% to 3.74%.
This increase is concurrent with the upstream search-cluster returning HTTP 503 errors.
The error rate increase is not explained by changes in request volume or latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a configuration change in service search.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase is observed in service search, not in other services.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a spike in user traffic.
ruled_out.reason: The request volume for service search did not change significantly.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a change in the infrastructure of service search.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase is observed in service search, not in other services.

The change is concentrated in service search: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.12).
At the same time, request volume for service search stayed about the same (2454 per 5 min before, 2862 per 5 min after, +17%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service search rose (141 ms before, 253 ms after, +80%).
